html:
The Battle of Acosta Ñu was fought on 16 August 1869 in central Paraguay, between a large Brazilian army and a Paraguayan force made up largely of boys and old men. The Paraguayans were wiped out.

By 1869 the War of the Triple Alliance was lost. Asunción had fallen, and Francisco Solano López was retreating into the hills with what remained of his army. To cover the retreat, a rearguard of a few thousand, many of them children, some said to have worn fake beards to look older, held the plain of Acosta Ñu for hours.

Most of them died or were captured. Paraguay keeps 16 August as Children's Day in their memory. The battle is the emblem of how completely the war consumed the country.
